claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The Orion spacecraft began its final descent at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
The Orion spacecraft endured a six-minute communications blackout due to extreme heat.
Artemis II reached Entry Interface at 400,000 feet at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
The communication blackout began at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Artemis II experienced peak heating or maximum plasma at approximately 5,000°F at 7:59 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Drogue parachutes deployed at 8:03 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Main parachutes deployed at 8:04 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II journey set a new record for human distance from Earth.
The Artemis II crew was recovered by the U.S. Navy and the USS John P. Murtha.
